Chapter 14: Enduring Faith—Holding On When the Road Is Long.
You know, there are moments when faith just feels easy. Prayers get answered, life is good, and hope seems to come naturally. But then there are those longer stretches—the seasons when the road feels endless, when doubts creep in, and honestly, it feels like just holding on is all you can do.
Enduring faith isn’t always something big or dramatic. Most of the time, it’s quiet and persistent—a determination that’s shaped in the middle of life’s toughest moments.
Imagine a couple, walking through years of infertility. Month after month, hope rises, only to be met with disappointment. Friends and family try to support them, but the deepest pain is something only they can carry. Still, they keep choosing faith—not because it’s easy, not because they always feel hopeful, but simply because they decide to trust, even when answers don’t come.
Or picture a man caring for his aging parent as dementia slowly takes hold. Every day, his patience is tested. The person he loves slips away just a little more, and grief mixes with exhaustion. But through it all, he finds a deeper well of compassion and resilience inside himself. For him, faith isn’t about having certainty. It’s about just being there—showing up, loving, and trusting that he’s not alone in this.
A lot of people expect faith to always feel strong or inspiring, but these stories show us something different. Real faith is often a choice—a decision to keep holding on, even when you don’t have the answers, and even when the path ahead is anything but clear.
So here’s the invitation: keep moving forward. Trust that you’re held, even in the messiest seasons. And remember, faith isn’t about knowing everything. It’s about choosing to believe, one small step at a time.
